**Subject: Electrical & electromechanical actuation for aerospace & defense (new build + retrofit) | Evidence base: Tier 2 public sources only, Sept 2021 – Sept 2026 | Compiled 4 Sept 2026**

## Key Insights

- **[High]** Published sizing for this market disagrees by up to 3.8× on identical nominal scope (USD 0.58bn vs USD 2.2bn for "EMA in aircraft," 2025) — so what: any landscape read anchored on a single vendor figure is structurally unreliable.
- **[High]** The July 2025 Safran/Collins transaction removed one of two direct competitors from the flight-control actuation tier and was accompanied by a regulator-forced divestiture of Safran's US EMA business — so what: the equipment tier consolidated and fragmented simultaneously, in different geographies.
- **[Medium]** Hydraulic actuation still held 44.90% of 2025 aircraft actuator revenue while electrical/EMA is the fastest-growing technology at a forecast 7.10% CAGR — so what: EMA is a share-shift story inside a growing base, not a replacement event.
- **[High]** A named Triumph engineering director states traditional commercial, military fixed-wing, vertical-lift and bizjet customers "do not see much changing with actuation," favouring proven hydraulics — so what: the pull for EMA is concentrated in new architectures and new platform classes, not the installed fleet.
- **[High]** Honeywell Aerospace identified ~2% of its supply base as constraining "hundreds of millions of dollars" of revenue — so what: near-term output in this market is supply-limited, not demand-limited.

## Industry Overview

**FACT [High]** — Safran closed the acquisition of Collins Aerospace's flight control and actuation activities on 21 July 2025 (~$1.55bn 2024 revenue, ~$130m EBITDA, USD 1.8bn enterprise value, 4,000 staff, 180 platforms) and simultaneously divested its ~$65m North American EMA business to Woodward to satisfy US regulators (Source: Safran press release, safran-group.com, 21 Jul 2025; Janes, 28 Jul 2025; FlightGlobal, 22 Jul 2025). *So what:* one transaction reset the supplier map for flight controls, wing fold, high-lift and thrust-vector actuation in a single day.

**FACT [Medium]** — By technology, hydraulic actuators retained 44.90% of 2025 aircraft actuator revenue; electrical and electromechanical units carry the highest forecast CAGR at 7.10% through 2031 (Source: Mordor Intelligence, mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/aircraft-actuators-market, Jul 2026). *So what:* the incumbent technology still funds the majority of the revenue pool that EMA programs are being developed against.

**OBSERVATION [High]** — Supply, not demand, is the binding constraint across the competitor set: Honeywell cites a 2% supplier subset limiting output; Safran cites raw materials, forging and casting (Sources: Motley Fool HONA Q2 2026 call transcript, 12 Aug 2026; Yahoo Finance/Safran FY25 call, 13 Feb 2026). *So what:* backlog conversion, not order capture, determines near-term revenue in both new-build and retrofit channels.

## Market Sizing — Triangulation

**External range (2025, all figures as published):**

| Source | Scope | 2025 est. (USD bn) | Relative scale |
|---|---|---|---|
| MarketsandMarkets | EMA in aircraft (component) | 0.58 | ▌ |
| Global Market Insights | EMA in aircraft | 2.20 | ████ |
| Fortune Business Insights | EMA, A&D incl. TVC/weapons | 2.70 | █████ |
| Mordor Intelligence | Aircraft actuators, all tech | 10.66 | ███████████████████ |
| Stratview Research | Aerospace actuators, all tech | 11.70 | █████████████████████ |
| Fortune Business Insights | Aircraft actuators, all tech | 24.40 | ███████████████████████████████████████████ |
| **Internal bottom-up (below)** | **A&D actuation, all tech, incl. missile/space** | **~15.0** | **██████████████████████████** |

**Internal bottom-up estimate — TAM.** Supplier roll-up, grossed up by published concentration:
1. Safran (acquired Collins A&FC) actuation revenue: **$1.55bn** (Source: Safran PR, 21 Jul 2025) — *sourced*.
2. Moog A&D revenue FY25: Commercial Aircraft $904m + Space & Defense $1,100m + Military Aircraft $888m = **$2.89bn** (Source: Moog 8-K, sec.gov, Nov 2025) — *sourced, arithmetic*.
3. Share of Moog A&D revenue attributable to actuation, control electronics and flight controls: **70%** — *ASSUMPTION*, based on Moog's published capability lists being dominated by actuation and control electronics across all four platform classes (Source: Moog capabilities catalogue via AeroExpo, n.d.).
4. Identified actuation revenue, two suppliers: $1.55bn + $2.02bn = **$3.57bn**.
5. These two represent roughly **half** of the combined top-5 actuation pool — *ASSUMPTION*; Honeywell, Parker and Liebherr do not disclose actuation revenue separately.
6. Top-5 hold **47.6%** of the market (Source: Global Market Insights, Jul 2026) — *sourced; EMA scope, applied here to actuation broadly as an ASSUMPTION*.
→ **TAM ≈ ($3.57bn × 2) ÷ 0.476 ≈ $15.0bn.**

**Reconciliation:** the estimate sits above the aircraft-only published range ($10.7–11.7bn) and below Fortune's $24.4bn, because it deliberately includes missile, space-launch and naval actuation that aircraft-scoped studies exclude. **Confidence: Low** — three chained assumptions, and exclusion of undisclosed Honeywell/Parker/Liebherr actuation biases it low while the concentration gross-up biases it high.

```
   ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │  TAM  ~$15.0bn  — global A&D actuation, all technologies,  │
   │  new-build + aftermarket, incl. missile/space/naval [Low]  │
   │   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
   │   │ SAM ~$2.5bn — electrical/EMA + integrated control│     │
   │   │ electronics, A&D, global, 2025 [Medium]          │     │
   │   │    ┌───────────────────────────────────┐        │     │
   │   │    │ SOM ~$103m/yr — 12 platform        │        │     │
   │   │    │ positions × $8.6m/platform [Low]   │        │     │
   │   │    └───────────────────────────────────┘        │     │
   │   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
   └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Formula footnotes.** **TAM** = (identified top-5 actuation revenue × 2) ÷ 47.6% top-5 share. **SAM** = midpoint of the two convergent A&D-scoped EMA estimates, GMI $2.2bn and Fortune $2.70bn (M&M's $0.58bn excluded as component-only outlier); cross-check — Moog's guided FY26 missile-actuation revenue of $275m equals ~11% of a $2.5bn EMA pool, plausible for one supplier in one application (Source: Yahoo Finance/Moog Q3 FY26 call, 1 Aug 2026). **SOM** = number of platform positions × annual revenue per platform, where revenue per platform = $1.55bn ÷ 180 platforms = **$8.6m/platform/yr** (derived from Safran PR, 21 Jul 2025); 12 positions is an *ILLUSTRATIVE ASSUMPTION*, not an observation.

*So what:* the electrical/EMA slice is roughly one-sixth of total A&D actuation spend, so EMA-specific plans built on all-technology actuator market figures overstate the reachable pool by ~6×.

| Missile / TVC actuation | Moog ~$275m FY26, +20% YoY | 🟩 [GROWTH] |
| Space / launch | Fortune: space & satellite segment 10.6% CAGR forecast | 🟨 [EMERGING] |
| AAM / eVTOL | Honeywell self-claim only; no third-party corroboration | 🟨 [EMERGING] |
| Hydraulic actuation | Losing share (44.90%), no source shows absolute decline | 🟦 [STABLE] |
| Full hydraulic→EMA fleet retrofit | "Airlines remain cautious about complete retrofits" (Mordor) | 🟧 [DECLINING/BLOCKED] |
| Warranty, list pricing, comparable specs | No public disclosure by any vendor | ⬜ [NO DATA] |

**Geography — FACT [High]:** North America held the largest share in 2025, corroborated at 42.00% by a second vendor (Sources: GMI, Jul 2026; Fortune Business Insights). **OBSERVATION [Medium]:** sources conflict on the fastest-growing region — GMI names Asia Pacific, MarketsandMarkets names Latin America. *So what:* growth-geography claims in this market are not yet corroborated and should be treated as single-source.

**FACT [High]** — Localisation is visible: Safran established a JV with Bharat Electronics in India (Source: Safran FY25 investor materials via Investing.com, 13 Feb 2026). *So what:* defense actuation demand is increasingly conditioned on in-country manufacture.

## Growth, Decline and Emerging Applications

**FACT [High]** — Airbus backlog reached 9,247 aircraft (May 2026), ~10.6 years of production coverage; Boeing BCA backlog rose to $567.3bn at 31 Dec 2025 (Sources: Forecast International, 10 Jun 2026; Boeing 10-K FY2025). *So what:* new-build actuation demand is contractually visible for a decade, subject to rate execution.

**OBSERVATION [Medium]** — Counter-signals exist at program level: A220 rate cut from 14 to 12/month for 2026, A350 constrained to six/month with A350F slipping to 2027, and Honeywell cut FY26 organic sales guidance from 7–9% to 4–5% (Sources: Forecast International, 12 Nov 2025 and 14 Jul 2026; Motley Fool HONA call, 12 Aug 2026). *So what:* aggregate backlog strength coexists with specific programs delivering below plan.

**UNKNOWN — declining markets.** No public source in this evidence base identifies a segment of aerospace EMA in absolute contraction. Hydraulic actuation is losing share, not volume. Missing: unit-volume time series by actuation technology.

**FACT [Medium/High]** — Emerging applications with hard evidence: ground-based air defense (Curtiss-Wright EMAs for Leidos, ~$40m), naval (Honeywell 48-actuator low-acoustic linear EMA system), missiles (Honeywell Assure; Moog PAC/THAAD rate expectations), CCA (150 aircraft awarded under Increment 1, ~$4.5bn, 2,350 possible in Increment 2 — analyst estimate), and hybrid electric-driven hydraulic power packs in landing gear bays (Sources: Interesting Engineering, ~Sep 2026; Honeywell product pages; Shephard Defence Insight; Aviation Week, 30 Aug 2023). *So what:* the fastest-emerging demand sits outside the commercial airframe applications that define most published market sizing.

## Confidence Summary

The consolidation narrative and the supplier financial anchors rest on **High-confidence** evidence — company press releases, SEC filings and earnings-call transcripts (Safran 21 Jul 2025 and 13 Feb 2026; Moog 8-K Nov 2025; Boeing 10-K; Honeywell Q2 2026). Segmentation shares, technology splits and regional rankings are **Medium** — single-vendor industry reports that disagree materially with one another. The TAM figure is **Low** confidence by construction: three assumptions are chained, and no public source discloses actuation revenue for Honeywell, Parker or Liebherr. Principal gaps: EMA shipset value per aircraft type, unit price points by application, replacement cycle/MTBUR, the new-build vs retrofit revenue split within EMA specifically, warranty terms, and any comparable cross-vendor performance specification. The most consequential single gap is shipset value — without it, a true platform × rate × content bottom-up cannot replace the concentration-based gross-up used here.
